headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Claude Code can modify shared repo state while emqx has broad network egress, creating leakage and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code ingests repo files, cwd, and user-provided directories by default, and can use MCP; emqx exposes HTTP API and broad network egress. If emqx outputs land in shared files or MCP-fed content, Claude Code may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF emqx writes untrusted content into a repo file or MCP-fed source that Claude Code reads
IF Claude Code parses emqx-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all emqx-generated text
Restrict Claude Code to a read-only review pass for emqx outputs
Disable MCP connections between the pair for untrusted content
Use a separate staging directory for any emqx output
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance metadata

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets in environment, while emqx handles IoT data and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files, Claude Code can read sensitive local data and emqx can transmit it outward. The shared-pathway risk is plausible from profiles alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or files
IF emqx forwards any file-derived content over its network egress
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from the shared cwd before running either agent
Block emqx egress for the shared workspace subnet
Rotate any exposed credentials after the run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state; emqx has broad network egress and HTTP API access. If both operate on the same mutable repo or directory, concurrent writes and git changes can collide, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. Because defaults are unsafe and loss can be irreversible, high fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git branch
IF emqx and Claude Code run concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories
Serialize writes with a manual lock file
Pause emqx while Claude Code edits the repo
Pause Claude Code while emqx publishes results
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code or analysis from repo context, and emqx can consume or relay HTTP/API data. If emqx treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or messages. The profiles do not show verification gates, but they also do not prove direct automation, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF emqx consumes Claude Code output without validation
IF Claude Code writes artifacts that emqx later republishes or acts on
mitigations: Require human review before emqx acts on Claude Code output
Add schema validation to all exchanged artifacts
Mark Claude Code output as draft-only
Limit emqx to read-only ingestion during the run
requires-engineering: implement verification and rollback hooks

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and local source code, while emqx is documented here only as touching IoT data. No residency or certification mismatch is shown, so only a limited compliance concern exists if regulated IoT data is routed into Claude Code's local terminal environment. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed from emqx into Claude Code
IF the shared workspace contains data subject to stricter retention than the local terminal environment
mitigations: Keep regulated IoT data out of the shared cwd
Redact identifiers before passing data to Claude Code
Document retention expectations for both tools
Use a separate compliance-approved staging area
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
